close_reason: documented N+2 gap, filed as MailBackend API gap
description: mailbox.rs handle_mailbox_set destroy path: for each mailbox destroyed with onDestroyRemoveEmails=true, the handler does query_objects + get_objects to find contained emails, then one destroy_object or update_object call per email. N emails = N+2 backend calls. A single destroy of a large inbox triggers hundreds of round-trips to storage. The comment in the code already notes this and suggests batch_destroy_objects/batch_update_objects. Without those traits, a user destroying a large Inbox with onDestroyRemoveEmails=true will see O(n) latency spikes visible to the HTTP client. This should be filed as a MailBackend API gap before the trait is frozen.
title: Mailbox/set destroy loop: N+2 backend calls per destroyed mailbox with emails
